record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of infinite dimensional algebras
record.original_question: Does there exist a finitely presented infinite torsion group, where a torsion group means a group in which every element has finite order?

evidence.quote: let G be a finitely generated torsion group, that is, for an arbitrary element g in G there exists n = n(g) > 1, such that g n = 1.
Problem 1. Do there exist infinite finitely presented torsion groups?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A group $G$ is called a torsion group (or periodic group) if every element $g \in G$ has finite order, i.e., there exists an integer $n = n(g) \geq 1$ such that $g^n = 1$. A group is finitely presented if it admits a presentation $\langle x_1, \dots, x_k \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ with finitely many generators and finitely many defining relations.

Question: Does there exist an infinite, finitely presented torsion group?
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of an infinite finitely presented torsion group is a well-known long-standing open problem in combinatorial/geometric group theory. While infinite finitely generated torsion groups have been constructed (Golod–Shafarevich, Aleshin, Grigorchuk; and the Burnside groups B(m,n) for large n by Novikov–Adian, Ol'shanskii, Ivanov, Lysenok), no example is known to be finitely presented, and the problem still appears in current problem lists (e.g., Baumslag's open problems in combinatorial group theory).

status_evidence.title: Open problems in combinatorial group theory (Baumslag et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the existence of an infinite finitely presented torsion group among open problems in combinatorial group theory.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as open in standard problem collections.

status_evidence.title: Torsion group - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Known infinite finitely generated torsion groups (Golod–Shafarevich, Grigorchuk, Burnside groups) are not known to be finitely presented.
status_evidence.claim: No known infinite torsion group has been shown to be finitely presented.
